skills.name: audit
skills.description: Use when an existing design, implementation or repository must be judged against stated quality attributes with evidence, rather than reviewed as a diff; not for reviewing a change (review) or for improving a measured metric (performance).

skills.name: blueprint
skills.description: Use when an accepted design must become concrete interfaces, files and signatures that an implementer can follow without re-deciding; not for choosing the design (design) or for ordering the work (plan).

skills.name: code-tour
skills.description: Use when someone needs to understand how existing code works — entry points, call path, state ownership — without changing it; not for explaining why a design was chosen (rationale) or for fixing it (debug).

skills.name: coverage
skills.description: Use when it is unclear whether the tests prove the acceptance criteria, or existing behaviour needs a safety net before change; not for writing the next test (tdd) or for running the gates (verify).

skills.name: debug
skills.description: Use when a failure is reproducible but its cause is unknown, and evidence must narrow it before any fix; not for interpreting a profile (forensics) or for fixing a known cause (tdd).

skills.name: decisions
skills.description: Record important decisions, pivots, failed approaches and evidence references

skills.name: design
skills.description: Use when a change needs its boundaries, interfaces and data flow decided before implementation, and the decision must survive review; not for ordering known work (plan) or for auditing a design that already exists (audit).

skills.name: evidence
skills.description: Use when a claim is about to be reported, committed or handed over and needs a recorded artifact behind it; not for producing the proof of a whole delivery (verify) or for writing the failing test (tdd).

skills.name: figure-it-out
skills.description: Use when no playbook fits and the situation needs a bespoke sequence built from skills, with the same guarantees as a playbook; not for work that matches an existing playbook (route) or a cause that is simply unknown (debug).

skills.name: forensics
skills.description: Use when a profile, trace, heap snapshot, log set or core dump must be interpreted into a cause; not for measuring an improvement (performance) or for reproducing a bug (debug).

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Create a complete worker-to-Lead or session-to-session handoff

skills.name: help
skills.description: Use when someone asks what the pack contains, which skill fits a task, or how to start using vstack; not for routing live work (route) or for a skill's own procedure.

skills.name: impact
skills.description: Use when a proposed change needs its blast radius known — callers, contracts, data, runtime effects — before work starts; not for deciding the change (design) or for verifying it after (verify).

skills.name: lessons
skills.description: Convert recurring mistakes into durable improvements

skills.name: migration
skills.description: Use when stored data, a public contract or a running system must move from one shape to another without a flag day; not for a fresh implementation (design) or a same-shape refactor (refactor).

skills.name: performance
skills.description: Use when a performance claim needs a baseline and a measured change under the same conditions; not for interpreting an existing profile (forensics) or for asserting speed without a number (evidence).

skills.name: plan
skills.description: Use when the work is framed and must be ordered into tasks with an artifact and a check each before coding starts; not for discovering what the problem is (shape) or for a situation with no known approach (figure-it-out).

skills.name: principles
skills.description: Use when a decision needs the rule behind it, or two reasonable approaches must be adjudicated before work continues; not for a skill's procedure (help) or a project's local conventions.

skills.name: prototype
skills.description: Use when a design question can only be answered by building something disposable and looking at it; not for answering a factual question (understand) or for production code (tdd).

skills.name: rationale
skills.description: Use when a decision's history must be reconstructed — what was chosen, what was rejected and on what evidence; not for how the code works now (code-tour) or for making a new decision (principles).

skills.name: ready
skills.description: Produce a merge-readiness assessment without merging

skills.name: recovery
skills.description: Restore a safe state after failed, interrupted or partially applied work

skills.name: red-team
skills.description: Use when a design or change needs an adversary that tries to break it before users or attackers do; not for checking it meets its spec (review) or for running the gates (verify).

skills.name: refactor
skills.description: Use when structure must change while behaviour stays exactly the same, and the safety net must exist before the first edit; not for changing behaviour (tdd) or moving a boundary other code depends on (design).

skills.name: report
skills.description: Produce a concise, source-grounded explanation for a developer, reviewer, or stakeholder from discovery findings

skills.name: resume
skills.description: Reconstruct current task or project context after interruption

skills.name: review
skills.description: Obtain fresh-context review and resolve findings

skills.name: route
skills.description: Use when a request arrives with no playbook open and the approach must be chosen before skills load; not for a one-file edit, a question a single read answers, or work whose route is already recorded.

skills.name: rubrics
skills.description: Use when a review needs explicit, checkable criteria instead of taste, or a pack artefact needs scoring against a fixed lens; not for performing the review itself (review) or judging whether gates pass (verify).

skills.name: shape
skills.description: Use when the request is understood but the problem is not framed — outcome, boundaries, unknowns and proof are still unstated; not for clarifying ambiguous wording (sharpen) or ordering known work (plan).

skills.name: sharpen
skills.description: Use when a request's wording is ambiguous, its acceptance criteria are missing, or its scope is stated as a feeling; not for framing a request that is already clear (shape) or ordering agreed work (plan).

skills.name: ship
skills.description: Prepare a focused, reviewable pull request with evidence

skills.name: skill-authoring
skills.description: Write skills to v2 contract standard: draft, static validation, external research, evaluation, lifecycle management

skills.name: skill-eval
skills.description: Evaluate skill trigger accuracy, procedure quality, outputs and failure handling through scenario-based testing

skills.name: tdd
skills.description: Use when behaviour must change and a test can state the expected behaviour before the implementation exists; not for characterising unknown existing behaviour (coverage) or for a disposable experiment (prototype).

skills.name: unslop
skills.description: Remove unnecessary complexity, duplication and low-quality generated changes

skills.name: unstick
skills.description: Use when the same failure has survived several fixes or the work keeps circling one assumption; not for a first debugging attempt (debug) or for a missing playbook (figure-it-out).

skills.name: verify
skills.description: Use when work claims to be complete and an independent run must prove it before merge, handoff or release; not for writing the failing test first (tdd) or recording one claim (evidence).

skills.name: verify-maintain
skills.description: Use when a project's verification commands may have drifted from the code, or a change alters how the project is checked; not for creating verification from scratch (verify-setup) or for running a delivery's gates (verify).

skills.name: verify-setup
skills.description: Use when a project has no reliable way to prove a change works and the verification instructions must be created and made runnable; not for running existing verification (verify) or for keeping it current (verify-maintain).

skills.name: visual-parity
skills.description: Use when a UI must match a defined reference — design file, previous build or specification — and the difference must be shown, not described; not for checking behaviour on a live page (browser-testing) or for a general review (review).

skills.name: watch-pr
skills.description: Monitor CI and review findings, then address and reverify valid issues

skills.name: worktree
skills.description: Establish, inspect and safely clean isolated workspaces
